tool_input.command:
mkdir -p forgemyspec-bundle/password-checker && cat > forgemyspec-board.yaml <<'EOF'
- id: R1
  status: doing
  title: "Password policy checker CLI"
  quote: "Build a password policy checker CLI in Python. Check a password against a configurable policy (minimum length, uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols, forbidden common passwords), report every failed rule, compute the Shannon entropy in bits, and generate random passwords that satisfy the policy. The policy can be loaded from policy.json; subcommands: check, generate, validate-policy. Single file password_checker.py, stdlib only."
  steps:
    - {do: "Spec written and lint passes", check: "cmd: PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/password-checker/spec.yaml --formal"}
    - {do: "User approves the spec bundle", ok: false}
    - {do: "Implement password_checker.py and tests until gate passes"}
EOF
cat > forgemyspec-bundle/password-checker/spec.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "0.1"
title: "Password policy checker CLI"
objective: "A single-file, stdlib-only Python CLI (password_checker.py) that checks passwords against a configurable policy, reports every failed rule, computes Shannon entropy, generates compliant random passwords, and validates policy files."
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: "Empty Python project; single module password_checker.py at the repository root, unittest tests in tests/, Python 3 stdlib only."
  assumptions:
    - "Policy fields: min_length (int >= 1), require_uppercase, require_lowercase, require_digits, require_symbols (booleans), forbidden_passwords (list of strings, compared case-insensitively)."
    - "Symbols are ASCII punctuation characters (string.punctuation)."
    - "Shannon entropy is the per-character empirical entropy H times the password length, in bits."
    - "The default policy path is policy.json in the current directory; --policy overrides it; with no file a built-in default policy applies."
    - "Exit codes: 0 success, 1 password fails policy, 2 invalid input or policy."
    - "Randomness comes from the secrets module."
constraints:
  - "Single file password_checker.py; Python standard library only, no third-party packages."
  - "No network access, no password storage or logging."
  - "Not a strength estimator beyond Shannon entropy; no breach-database lookup."
  - "The password is never echoed in the output of check."
success_criteria:
  - "check reports every failed rule in one run, not only the first."
  - "check prints the Shannon entropy in bits and exits 0 when compliant, 1 when not."
  - "generate outputs passwords that pass check under the same policy."
  - "validate-policy accepts a valid policy.json and rejects an invalid one with a message naming the problem."
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "check evaluates min length, uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol and forbidden-password rules and lists every failed rule.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h2, description: "Shannon entropy in bits is computed correctly for any password.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h3, description: "generate returns random passwords that satisfy every rule of the policy.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h4, description: "The policy is loaded from policy.json and validate-policy rejects malformed policies.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h5, description: "The CLI exposes the subcommands check, generate and validate-policy with documented exit codes.", confidence: 0.9}
required_evidence:
  - "unittest run of tests/ passing, including each boundary obligation test"
  - "Command output of check, generate and validate-policy against a sample policy.json"
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Design the policy schema and CLI interface", type: design, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h4, h5]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Implement rule checking and entropy", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Implement generator", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h3]}
  - {id: a4, description: "Implement policy loading, validation and the CLI", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h4, h5]}
  - {id: a5, description: "Run tests and the gate", type: validate, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]}
decision_rules:
  - "If the policy is unsatisfiable (e.g. min_length smaller than the number of required classes, or a required class impossible), validate-policy rejects it."
  - "Ask the user before adding any rule or dependency beyond this spec."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a password policy checker CLI in Python. Check a password against a configurable policy (minimum length, uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols, forbidden common passwords), report every failed rule, compute the Shannon entropy in bits, and generate random passwords that satisfy the policy. The policy can be loaded from policy.json; subcommands: check, generate, validate-policy. Single file password_checker.py, stdlib only."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "report every failed rule"
      - "Shannon entropy in bits"
      - "generate random passwords that satisfy the policy"
      - "policy loaded from policy.json"
      - "subcommands check, generate, validate-policy"
      - "single file password_checker.py, stdlib only"
formal:
  module: PasswordChecker
  obligations:
    - id: all_failures_reported
      kind: boundary
      statement: "check evaluates min length, uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols and forbidden passwords, and lists every failed rule in one run."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["report every failed rule"]
      test: "test_password_checker.CheckTests.test_reports_every_failed_rule"
    - id: entropy_bits
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Shannon entropy is length times per-character empirical entropy; 'aaaa' is 0 bits and 'abcd' is 8 bits."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["Shannon entropy in bits"]
      test: "test_password_checker.EntropyTests.test_known_values"
    - id: generate_satisfies_policy
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Generated passwords pass check under the same policy, over many runs and varied policies."
      hypotheses: [h3]
      must_include: ["generate random passwords that satisfy the policy"]
      test: "test_password_checker.GenerateTests.test_generated_passwords_pass_policy"
    - id: policy_from_file
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The policy is read from policy.json (or --policy path); a missing or malformed file exits 2."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["policy loaded from policy.json"]
      test: "test_password_checker.PolicyTests.test_loads_policy_json"
    - id: validate_policy_rejects_invalid
      kind: boundary
      statement: "validate-policy exits 0 for a valid policy and 2 with a message naming the field for an invalid or unsatisfiable one."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["policy loaded from policy.json"]
      test: "test_password_checker.PolicyTests.test_validate_policy_rejects_invalid"
    - id: cli_subcommands
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The CLI has check, generate and validate-policy; check exits 0 if compliant and 1 otherwise; unknown subcommand exits 2."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["subcommands check, generate, validate-policy"]
      test: "test_password_checker.CliTests.test_subcommands_and_exit_codes"
    - id: single_file_stdlib
      kind: boundary
      statement: "password_checker.py is one file importing only standard library modules."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["single file password_checker.py, stdlib only"]
      test: "test_password_checker.StructureTests.test_only_stdlib_imports"
scope:
  paths: ["password_checker.py", "tests/**", "policy.json"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
EOF
export PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness
python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/password-checker/spec.yaml --formal && python3 -m forgemyspec package forgemyspec-bundle/password-checker/spec.yaml && python3 -m forgemyspec board start R1 && python3 -m forgemyspec board

result:
The spec is written and lint passes (100/100, 0 errors, 0 warnings), but I haven't written any code yet. I need your approval first.

**Spec-only bundle:** `forgemyspec-bundle/password-checker/`. I chose spec-only because this is an ordinary feature, not a case that needs Dafny proofs. Every obligation is tested at the boundary instead.

| Obligation | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `all_failures_reported` | `check` evaluates the six rules (min length, uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols, forbidden passwords) and lists every failed one. |
| `entropy_bits` | Shannon entropy is the length times the per-character entropy. `aaaa` gives 0 bits and `abcd` gives 8 bits. |
| `generate_satisfies_policy` | Generated passwords pass `check` under the same policy. |
| `policy_from_file` | The policy loads from `policy.json`, or from a `--policy` path. A missing or malformed file exits 2. |
| `validate_policy_rejects_invalid` | `validate-policy` exits 0 for a valid policy. For an invalid or unsatisfiable one it exits 2 and names the field. |
| `cli_subcommands` | The CLI has `check`, `generate` and `validate-policy`. `check` exits 0 if compliant and 1 if not. An unknown subcommand exits 2. |
| `single_file_stdlib` | `password_checker.py` is one file and imports only the standard library. |

**Assumptions I made. Please confirm or correct them:**
- Policy fields are `min_length`, `require_uppercase`, `require_lowercase`, `require_digits`, `require_symbols` and `forbidden_passwords`.
- The forbidden-password comparison is case-insensitive.
- Symbols are ASCII punctuation (`string.punctuation`).
- Entropy is the empirical per-character entropy times the length.
- With no `policy.json`, a built-in default policy applies.
- Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for a password that fails the policy, and 2 for invalid input or policy.
- Generation uses the `secrets` module.
- `check` never echoes the password.
- `validate-policy` rejects a policy that can't be satisfied, such as a `min_length` smaller than the number of required character classes.
